title: The ENTIRE Israel, Palestine and Iran Conflict, Explained
keyword: israel palestine conflict explained / iran israel war explained / middle east war explained
rule: Neutralidad estricta: cada afirmación disputada va atribuida; tiempo parejo para israelíes, palestinos e iraníes. Datos: Datos (Codex).md.

scenes.headline: FEB 28, 2026
scenes.text: On the 28th of February 2026, American and Israeli strikes killed the man who had ruled Iran for 36 years.
scenes.visual: Cuadro 0: relieve 3D de Irán de noche, estelas de misiles ya en el aire; impacto en 'killed' (sin cuerpos), temblor. Etiqueta ANIMATED RECONSTRUCTION.

scenes.headline: HORMUZ
scenes.text: Iran fired missiles at Israel and at Gulf states hosting American bases. Then it began closing the Strait of Hormuz, the route for about a fifth of the world's oil.
scenes.visual: Cámara vuela del Golfo al estrecho de Ormuz 3D: petroleros se detienen en fila; contador 20% OF WORLD OIL.

scenes.headline: HOW?
scenes.text: So how did a fight over land only a little larger than New Jersey drag in Iran, America and the world's oil? And why does every ceasefire seem to break?
scenes.visual: Mapa neón alejándose: Israel y los territorios palestinos diminutos, silueta de New Jersey superpuesta a escala (algo mayor que NJ); luego Irán, EE. UU. y rutas de petróleo se encienden. Dos signos de pregunta.

scenes.headline: ONE BUILDING
scenes.text: To answer that, we have to start with one building in Tehran. In February 1979, the flag on it changed.
scenes.visual: Edificio Stick de embajada en Teherán; una bandera genérica azul baja y sube otra genérica verde-roja-negra (sin emblemas). Reloj 1979.

scenes.text: Why it changed is part of a story that starts thirty years earlier, with two peoples claiming the same land. This is that whole story, told from every side.
scenes.visual: Línea de tiempo 1948 → 2026 que se dibuja; tres Sticks (israelí, palestino, iraní) aparecen de igual tamaño, uno junto al otro.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER I
scenes.text: Chapter one. One land, two peoples.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo sobre el mapa neón del Mediterráneo oriental.

scenes.headline: WHY THIS LAND?
scenes.text: For many Jews, this was an ancestral homeland and a hoped-for refuge from persecution. Palestinian Arabs also had deep ties to the land, where their families had lived for generations, and wanted a nation of their own. Both peoples claimed a national future in the same place.
scenes.visual: Mapa neón; dos líneas de tiempo paralelas suben desde la misma tierra: un Stick judío con maleta llegando, un Stick palestino junto a un olivo. Mismo tamaño.

scenes.text: After the Second World War, Britain was ready to leave the land it had ruled as Mandatory Palestine. Jews and Arabs both lived there, and both wanted it as their home.
scenes.visual: Mapa del Mandato en neón; Stick británico se va en barco; dos Sticks (judío, árabe) parados sobre el mismo mapa.

scenes.text: In November 1947, the United Nations voted on a plan to split it into two states, a Jewish one and an Arab one, with Jerusalem under international control. Thirty-three countries voted yes, thirteen voted no, and ten abstained.
scenes.visual: Tablero de votación 33/13/10 que se llena; el mapa se divide en dos colores con Jerusalén en un círculo neutro.

scenes.headline: YES / NO
scenes.text: Jewish leaders accepted the plan as a path to a state. Arab leaders rejected it, arguing that the Arab majority should decide the future of the whole land.
scenes.visual: Pantalla dividida: Stick líder judío asiente con un papel; Stick líder árabe niega con la mano. Mismo tamaño, mismo encuadre.

scenes.headline: MAY 1948
scenes.text: Fighting broke out. In May 1948, Israel declared independence, and the next day the armies of neighbouring Arab states entered the war.
scenes.visual: Estrella de 'independencia' aparece sobre Israel (sin símbolos); flechas de ejércitos árabes entran desde Egipto, Jordania, Siria, Líbano, Irak.

scenes.headline: TWO NAMES
scenes.text: Israelis remember this as their War of Independence. Palestinians call it the Nakba, the catastrophe. Around 700,000 to 750,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes.
scenes.visual: Dos placas con los dos nombres, mismo tamaño; columna de pequeños Sticks con maletas que cruza el mapa; contador 700,000–750,000.

scenes.text: When the fighting stopped in 1949, Israel held about 77 percent of the land. Egypt ran the Gaza Strip, and Jordan held the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. The Arab state from the UN plan never appeared.
scenes.visual: Mapa 1949: Israel 77%, Gaza (Egipto), Cisjordania (Jordania) con etiquetas; un recuadro punteado 'ARAB STATE' se desvanece.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER II
scenes.text: Chapter two. Occupation, uprising, and a handshake.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo.

scenes.headline: MAY 1967
scenes.text: By 1967 the region was tense again. Egypt moved troops into the Sinai and closed the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping. Israeli leaders feared a wider war.
scenes.visual: Flechas egipcias entran al Sinaí; un candado se cierra sobre el estrecho de Tirán; Stick israelí mira el mapa.

scenes.headline: 6 DAYS
scenes.text: In June 1967, after weeks of rising tension with its neighbours, Israel struck first. In just six days it took Gaza and the Sinai from Egypt, the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan, and the Golan Heights from Syria.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D: relieve de la región, cámara alta; las cuatro zonas se iluminan una por una con contador de días 1→6.

scenes.headline: SINAI RETURNED
scenes.text: Israel later gave the Sinai back to Egypt in exchange for peace. But Gaza and the West Bank, home to millions of Palestinians, stayed under Israeli military control.
scenes.visual: Sinaí vuelve al color de Egipto con un apretón de manos Stick; Gaza y Cisjordania quedan rayadas 'ISRAELI MILITARY CONTROL'.

scenes.headline: SETTLEMENTS
scenes.text: Over the following decades, Israel built settlements there. Today roughly 740,000 to 780,000 Israeli settlers live in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. The UN's top court says these settlements break international law. Israel rejects that and says the land's future must be negotiated.
scenes.visual: Puntitos de asentamientos que aparecen en Cisjordania con el paso de los años; contador; dos burbujas de posición: ICJ / ISRAEL.

scenes.headline: INTIFADA
scenes.text: In 1987, Palestinians rose up against Israeli rule in what became known as the First Intifada, meaning shaking off. Strikes, protests and stone-throwing went on for years.
scenes.visual: Multitud de Sticks palestinos con carteles en blanco frente a Sticks soldados; sin heridos. Palabra 'INTIFADA = SHAKING OFF'.

scenes.headline: DAILY LIFE
scenes.text: Over the following decades, for many Palestinians, life under occupation meant checkpoints, permits and soldiers at the end of the street. For many Israelis, it meant fear of attacks on buses and cafés. Civilians in both societies faced fear, loss and insecurity.
scenes.visual: Pantalla dividida igual: Stick palestino en fila de control; Stick israelí esperando un autobús mirando alrededor. Sin violencia.

scenes.text: Then came a surprise. In 1993, Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization exchanged letters. The PLO recognised Israel. Israel recognised the PLO as the representative of the Palestinian people.
scenes.visual: Dos cartas cruzan el mapa en direcciones opuestas: 'PLO → ISRAEL' y 'ISRAEL → PLO'.

scenes.headline: OSLO
scenes.text: These were the Oslo Accords. They created the Palestinian Authority to govern parts of Gaza and the West Bank for five years, while the hardest questions were left for later: borders, Jerusalem, refugees and settlements.
scenes.visual: Apretón de manos Stick frente a la Casa Blanca estilizada; reloj de arena '5 YEARS'; cuatro cajas cerradas: BORDERS, JERUSALEM, REFUGEES, SETTLEMENTS.

scenes.headline: LATER?
scenes.text: Later never really came.
scenes.visual: El reloj de arena se vacía; las cuatro cajas siguen cerradas y se cubren de polvo.

scenes.headline: NOV 1995
scenes.text: In 1995, Israel's prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, who had signed Oslo, was shot dead at a peace rally by an Israeli extremist who opposed the deal. His murder deepened the crisis facing a peace process already shaken by opposition and violence.
scenes.visual: Plaza de noche con globos de un mitin; un foco se apaga sobre el podio vacío (sin mostrar el disparo). Dos balanzas se inclinan hacia los extremos.

scenes.headline: CAMP DAVID
scenes.text: In the summer of 2000, American president Bill Clinton brought Israeli and Palestinian leaders to Camp David to settle everything at once. After two weeks, they left without a final agreement, and each side blamed the other for the failure.
scenes.visual: Cabaña en el bosque; dos Sticks líderes y Stick Clinton en la mesa; reloj 14 días; se van por puertas opuestas con burbujas de culpa del mismo tamaño.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER III
scenes.text: Chapter three. The flag in Tehran.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo; cámara viaja del Mediterráneo a Irán.

scenes.headline: QUIET PARTNERS
scenes.text: Now back to that building. Before 1979, Iran was ruled by a king, the Shah. Iran and Israel were quiet partners, sharing intelligence, trade and military cooperation, even without a formal alliance.
scenes.visual: Stick Sha con corona sencilla y Stick israelí intercambian una carpeta bajo la mesa; línea punteada Teherán–Tel Aviv.

scenes.headline: REVOLUTION
scenes.text: Then, in 1979, a revolution swept the Shah away, and Iran became an Islamic Republic. Its new leaders made opposition to Israel part of the state's mission.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D de una calle de Teherán estilizada con multitud de figuras simples; el retrato del Sha cae (cartel genérico). Corte a Stick ayatolá (sin texto).

scenes.headline: 444 DAYS
scenes.text: That same year, Iranian students stormed the American embassy in Tehran and held 52 Americans hostage for 444 days. Iran's revolutionary leaders turned openly hostile to both America and Israel.
scenes.visual: Embajada estadounidense estilizada; contador 444 DAYS; dos etiquetas aparecen sobre los mapas de EE. UU. e Israel.

scenes.headline: SAME BUILDING
scenes.text: Iran cut ties with Israel. And the Israeli embassy in Tehran was handed over to the PLO. The same building, a different flag. Iran's new leaders made the Palestinian cause part of their foreign policy.
scenes.visual: Vuelve el edificio de la escena 004; cambia la bandera; un hilo rojo une Teherán con Gaza y Cisjordania en el mapa.

scenes.text: In 1982, Israel invaded Lebanon to drive out PLO fighters. Iran's Revolutionary Guards went to Lebanon too, and helped found a new Shia group there: Hezbollah. Iran trained it, armed it and paid for it.
scenes.visual: Flecha israelí entra en Líbano; flecha iraní llega por Siria; aparece un punto 'HEZBOLLAH 1982' que crece.

scenes.headline: NOT OVERNIGHT
scenes.text: Even so, the break was not overnight. During Iran's long war with Iraq in the 1980s, Israel still quietly sold Western weapons to Iran. Enemies in public, sometimes partners in secret.
scenes.visual: Stick israelí pasa una caja con 'WEAPONS' bajo la mesa a Stick iraní mientras ambos se gritan en público.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER IV
scenes.text: Chapter four. Walls, rockets and centrifuges.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo.

scenes.text: In 2000, peace talks collapsed and a Second Intifada began. This time it was far deadlier, Palestinian bombings and shootings killed Israelis, including civilians. Israeli military operations killed Palestinians, including civilians. It lasted about five years.
scenes.visual: Mesa de negociación que se parte; línea de tiempo 2000–2005 con iconos simples (alarma, tanque), sin víctimas.

scenes.headline: THE BARRIER
scenes.text: During those years, Israel began building a barrier of fences and concrete walls along and inside the West Bank. Israel says it stopped bombers from getting through. Palestinians say it cut them off from their land, and in 2004 the UN's top court called the parts inside the West Bank illegal.
scenes.visual: Línea del muro sobre Cisjordania, a veces sobre la línea de 1967 y a veces dentro; dos burbujas iguales; sello ICJ 2004.

scenes.text: In 2005, Israel pulled all 21 of its settlements and its permanent troops out of Gaza. About 8,500 settlers left.
scenes.visual: Los 21 puntos de Gaza desaparecen uno por uno; camiones Stick salen hacia Israel; contador 21 → 0.

scenes.headline: HAMAS
scenes.text: A year later, Hamas, an Islamist movement that refuses to recognise Israel, won Palestinian parliamentary elections. In 2007, after fighting its rival Fatah, it took full control of Gaza. Fatah's Palestinian Authority kept governing parts of the West Bank.
scenes.visual: Urna con '74 / 132'; el mapa palestino se divide: Gaza color Hamas, Cisjordania color Autoridad Palestina.

scenes.headline: BLOCKADE
scenes.text: Israel tightened a blockade around Gaza, and Egypt restricted its own border crossing. Israel said it was stopping weapons from reaching Hamas. Palestinians called it collective punishment of two million people.
scenes.visual: Línea de bloqueo alrededor de Gaza (Israel) y paso de Rafah (Egipto) en otro color; dos burbujas de posición del mismo tamaño.

scenes.text: Rockets from Gaza and Israeli strikes became a cycle. There were major wars in 2008, 2014 and 2021, each ending in a ceasefire that solved nothing underneath.
scenes.visual: Tres arcos de cohetes y tres de ataques aéreos que se repiten; contador de años; cada vez aparece 'CEASEFIRE' y se borra.

scenes.headline: 15 SECONDS
scenes.text: In Israeli towns near Gaza, families had about fifteen seconds to reach a shelter when the sirens went off. In Gaza, two million people lived behind the blockade, most unable to leave, with power cuts for much of the day.
scenes.visual: Pantalla dividida: cronómetro 15s con familia Stick corriendo al refugio / Gaza de noche con luces que se apagan por barrios.

scenes.headline: NATANZ
scenes.text: Meanwhile, the fight with Iran moved underground. Iran was enriching uranium at a site called Natanz. In 2010, a computer worm named Stuxnet was found inside, built to sabotage the machines that spin the uranium.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D: sala subterránea con filas de centrifugadoras girando; un código verde se mete y algunas empiezan a tambalearse.

scenes.headline: THE DEAL
scenes.text: In 2015, Iran and world powers signed a deal. Iran limited its enrichment and accepted inspections, in exchange for relief from sanctions. In 2018, President Trump pulled America out and brought the sanctions back.
scenes.visual: Firma del acuerdo con 3.67% en una etiqueta; luego Stick Trump rompe su copia; las cadenas de sanciones vuelven a Irán.

scenes.headline: SHADOW WAR
scenes.text: Then came the shadow war: sabotage, cyberattacks and assassinations. In 2020, Iran's top nuclear scientist was killed near Tehran. Iran blamed Israel. Israel did not claim it.
scenes.visual: Mapa nocturno con siluetas que se mueven; carretera cerca de Teherán; dos burbujas: IRAN: ISRAEL DID IT / ISRAEL: NO COMMENT.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER V
scenes.text: Chapter five. October the 7th, and the war in Gaza.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo; fondo más oscuro.

scenes.headline: OCT 7, 2023
scenes.text: On the 7th of October 2023, Hamas-led fighters broke through the fence around Gaza and attacked towns, army posts and a music festival in southern Israel.
scenes.visual: Mapa: la línea de la valla de Gaza se rompe en varios puntos; flechas hacia el sur de Israel; íconos de pueblo y festival. Sin violencia gráfica.

scenes.text: According to Israel, about 1,200 people were killed, most of them civilians, and 251 people were taken back into Gaza as hostages. It was the deadliest day in Israel's history.
scenes.visual: Dos contadores sobrios en blanco: 1,200 KILLED y 251 HOSTAGES; fuente 'ISRAELI TALLY'.

scenes.headline: WAR
scenes.text: Israel declared war, with two goals: destroy Hamas and bring the hostages home. What followed was a massive air and ground campaign in one of the most crowded places on Earth.
scenes.visual: Gaza en primer plano; dos casillas: DESTROY HAMAS / BRING HOSTAGES HOME; flechas terrestres entran desde el norte.

scenes.headline: NOV 2023
scenes.text: In late November 2023, a one-week truce freed more than a hundred hostages in exchange for Palestinian prisoners. Then the fighting resumed, and moved south.
scenes.visual: Reloj de 7 días; autobuses Stick cruzan en ambas direcciones; luego la flecha militar baja hacia Jan Yunis y Rafah.

scenes.text: By late November 2026, Gaza's Health Ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, reported at least 74,746 Palestinians killed. Its count does not separate civilians from fighters, and Israel disputes it.
scenes.visual: Contador sobrio 74,746 con la fuente atribuida debajo; burbuja ISRAEL DISPUTES. Sin imágenes de víctimas.

scenes.headline: 90% DISPLACED
scenes.text: Nearly 1.9 million people, about nine in ten Gazans, were driven from their homes, many of them again and again.
scenes.visual: Cuadrícula de 10 Sticks: 9 se mueven con maletas por el mapa de Gaza, de norte a sur y de vuelta.

scenes.headline: FAMINE?
scenes.text: In August 2025, the UN-backed food experts of the IPC confirmed famine in Gaza City and the area around it. Israel rejected the finding and challenged the data.
scenes.visual: Termómetro IPC que sube a la fase 5 sobre la gobernación de Gaza; burbuja ISRAEL REJECTS al lado, mismo tamaño.

scenes.headline: THE COURT
scenes.text: South Africa took Israel to the International Court of Justice, accusing it of genocide. Israel denies it and says it is defending itself against Hamas. The court ordered Israel to prevent genocidal acts, but it has not ruled on the accusation itself. That decision is still years away.
scenes.visual: Sala del tribunal estilizada; Stick Sudáfrica y Stick Israel en estrados iguales; calendario que pasa a 2027… 2029.

scenes.headline: OCT 2024
scenes.text: In October 2024, Israeli troops killed Yahya Sinwar, the Hamas leader in Gaza who had planned October 7th. The war did not stop.
scenes.visual: Marcador en Rafah; retrato Stick genérico de Sinwar se apaga; el contador de la guerra sigue corriendo.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER VI
scenes.text: Chapter six. The ring of fire.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo; mapa amplio de Medio Oriente.

scenes.headline: THE AXIS
scenes.text: Around Israel stood groups backed by Iran: Hezbollah in Lebanon, militias in Iraq and Syria, the Houthis in Yemen, and Hamas itself. Iran calls them the axis of resistance. Each has its own leaders and its own goals, but Iran helped arm them all.
scenes.visual: Anillo neón alrededor de Israel con nodos: LEBANON, SYRIA, IRAQ, YEMEN, GAZA; líneas finas hacia Irán. Etiqueta 'AXIS OF RESISTANCE (Iran's name)'.

scenes.headline: THE NORTH
scenes.text: The day after October 7th, Hezbollah began firing at northern Israel in support of Gaza. Israel fired back. Tens of thousands of people on both sides of the border had to leave their homes.
scenes.visual: Frontera Israel–Líbano: arcos en ambas direcciones; pequeños Sticks evacuando a ambos lados, mismo número.

scenes.headline: THE PAGERS
scenes.text: Then, in September 2024, thousands of pagers used by Hezbollah members exploded almost at the same moment. The next day, it was walkie-talkies. Israel's prime minister later confirmed he had approved the operation.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D macro: un pager sobre una mesa vibra y su pantalla parpadea; corte a mapa con cientos de destellos simultáneos en Líbano. Sin lesiones.

scenes.headline: NASRALLAH
scenes.text: Ten days later, an Israeli airstrike in Beirut killed Hassan Nasrallah, Hezbollah's leader for 32 years.
scenes.visual: Zoom a Beirut; marcador del ataque; retrato Stick genérico de Nasrallah (turbante negro, barba) se apaga.

scenes.headline: INTO LEBANON
scenes.text: Israeli troops then crossed into southern Lebanon. In late November 2024, a ceasefire ended the main fighting, though Israeli strikes in Lebanon continued, with Israel saying it was targeting Hezbollah.
scenes.visual: Flechas israelíes entran al sur del Líbano; letrero CEASEFIRE NOV 2024; pequeños destellos esporádicos.

scenes.headline: RED SEA
scenes.text: Far to the south, the Houthis in Yemen started attacking ships in the Red Sea, saying they were acting for the Palestinians. Shipping companies sent their vessels the long way around Africa. Traffic through the strait off Yemen fell by more than half.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D: portacontenedores en el mar Rojo da la vuelta; cámara sube y se ve la ruta larga alrededor de África. Contador −55% TRANSITS.

scenes.headline: ASSAD FALLS
scenes.text: And in December 2024, rebels toppled Bashar al-Assad in Syria. Iran lost its land bridge to Hezbollah. In just a few months, Iran's ring had been badly broken.
scenes.visual: La línea Irán→Irak→Siria→Líbano se corta en Siria; los nodos del anillo parpadean y varios se apagan.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER VII
scenes.text: Chapter seven. Face to face.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo.

scenes.headline: APRIL 2024
scenes.text: For forty-five years, Iran and Israel had fought through others. That ended in April 2024. After a strike on Iran's embassy compound in Damascus, widely blamed on Israel, Iran launched more than 300 drones and missiles straight at Israel.
scenes.visual: Mapa: punto en Damasco; desde Irán salen 300 trazos que cruzan Irak y Jordania; contador 300+.

scenes.headline: INTERCEPTED
scenes.text: Most were shot down by Israel and its allies, and Israel answered with a limited strike.
scenes.visual: La mayoría de los trazos se apagan con destellos de intercepción; segundo ciclo de flechas en ambos sentidos, mismo peso visual.

scenes.headline: TEHRAN, JULY 2024
scenes.text: Then, in July, Hamas's political leader, Ismail Haniyeh, was killed in a guesthouse in Tehran, where he had come for the new Iranian president's inauguration. Iran blamed Israel and promised retaliation. Months later, Israel's defence minister acknowledged the killing.
scenes.visual: Zoom a Teherán de noche; casa de huéspedes estilizada; un punto se apaga; burbuja IRAN: RETALIATION / luego ISRAEL ACKNOWLEDGES (dic 2024).

scenes.headline: OCT 2024
scenes.text: In October, Iran fired about 180 ballistic missiles at Israel. Weeks later, Israel struck military targets inside Iran.
scenes.visual: Segundo ciclo de flechas: 180 trazos desde Irán; luego flechas israelíes a bases iraníes; mismo peso visual.

scenes.headline: JUNE 13, 2025
scenes.text: Then, on the 13th of June 2025, Israel launched a much bigger attack on Iran's nuclear sites, missile bases and military commanders. Israel said Iran was getting dangerously close to a nuclear weapon.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D: relieve de Irán, cazas cruzan el cielo hacia instalaciones con cúpulas; burbuja ISRAEL: NUCLEAR THREAT.

scenes.text: Iran said its program was peaceful. It had enriched uranium to sixty percent, far beyond what power plants use, but having that material is not the same as having a bomb.
scenes.visual: Barra de enriquecimiento: 3.67% (deal) → 60% → 90% (weapons grade, línea punteada sin alcanzar); burbuja IRAN: PEACEFUL.

scenes.headline: FORDOW
scenes.text: Iran fired waves of missiles at Israeli cities. On the 22nd of June, America joined in, bombing three nuclear sites, including Fordow, buried deep inside a mountain.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D: montaña de Fordow en corte, bombas penetrantes bajan por la roca; impacto contenido. Luego flechas de misiles hacia Israel.

scenes.headline: 12 DAYS
scenes.text: After twelve days, a ceasefire announced by Washington took hold. Iran reported about 1,062 people killed. Israel reported 29. Nobody could say for sure how much of Iran's nuclear program survived underground.
scenes.visual: Contador de días 1→12; dos contadores sobrios con sus fuentes; signo de pregunta sobre Fordow.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER VIII
scenes.text: Chapter eight. Deals that don't hold.
scenes.visual: Tarjeta de capítulo.

scenes.headline: JAN 2025
scenes.text: In Gaza, a ceasefire in January 2025 swapped 33 Israeli hostages, living and dead, for nearly 1,800 Palestinian prisoners. In March, Israel resumed its strikes. Israel blamed Hamas for refusing more releases. Hamas said Israel had abandoned the deal's second phase.
scenes.visual: Balanza de intercambio 33 ↔ ~1,800; reloj 42 días; luego se rompe; dos burbujas de culpa del mismo tamaño.

scenes.headline: OCT 2025
scenes.text: In October 2025, a new ceasefire under President Trump's twenty-point plan brought the last living hostages home and let more aid in. Israeli troops pulled back part of the way.
scenes.visual: Lista de 20 casillas; algunas se marcan; camiones de ayuda entran; la línea de tropas retrocede parcialmente.

scenes.headline: STALLED
scenes.text: But the harder steps stalled: disarming Hamas, a full Israeli withdrawal, an international force, and rebuilding. Strikes and deaths continued, each side blaming the other.
scenes.visual: Cuatro casillas sin marcar: DISARM HAMAS, FULL WITHDRAWAL, STABILIZATION FORCE, REBUILD; pequeñas chispas que siguen en el mapa.

scenes.text: And then, Iran. After the February strikes, a ceasefire came in April. America blockaded Iran's ports. In June, both sides signed a sixty-day deal and the blockade was lifted.
scenes.visual: Línea de tiempo 2026: FEB STRIKES → APR CEASEFIRE → APR BLOCKADE → JUN DEAL; barcos estadounidenses rodean puertos iraníes y luego se retiran.

scenes.headline: BLOCKADE BACK
scenes.text: Within weeks, attacks on ships and new American strikes broke it. The blockade came back in July. As of late November 2026, talks continue in Qatar, and Iran is still closing Hormuz one day at a time.
scenes.visual: Toma 3D reutilizada de Ormuz (escena 002) con la flota de bloqueo de regreso; calendario que pasa día a día.

scenes.headline: CHAPTER IX
scenes.text: So why doesn't it end?
scenes.visual: Mapa completo de la región con todos los frentes encendidos a la vez.

scenes.headline: ISRAEL'S GOVERNMENT
scenes.text: Israel's government says it cannot be safe while Hamas is armed on its border, or while Iran can build missiles and get close to a bomb. It opposes a Palestinian state now, saying that would reward October 7th.
scenes.visual: Stick gobierno israelí con tres tarjetas: HAMAS ARMED, IRAN MISSILES, NO STATE NOW.

scenes.headline: PALESTINIAN LEADERS
scenes.text: The Palestinian Authority wants a state on the 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital, living in peace beside Israel. Its president has rejected October 7th and says Hamas must give up its weapons. Hamas demands a permanent end to the war and a full Israeli withdrawal.
scenes.visual: Dos Sticks palestinos separados (Autoridad Palestina / Hamas), cada uno con sus tarjetas; mapa 1967 con Jerusalén Este.

scenes.headline: IRAN'S GOVERNMENT
scenes.text: Iran's government says it will never build a nuclear weapon, but it wants to keep enriching uranium, and it demands an end to the blockade, the sanctions and the attacks. Meanwhile, ordinary Iranian families live with the strikes and an economy squeezed by sanctions.
scenes.visual: Stick gobierno iraní con tarjetas: NO BOMB, KEEP ENRICHING, END BLOCKADE.

scenes.headline: THE ANSWER
scenes.text: So how did a strip of land pull in Iran, America and the world's oil? Because since 1979, the fight over that land and the conflict between Iran and Israel have been linked. And why do the ceasefires break? Because questions of security, land, sovereignty and power are still unresolved, and each government sees the other's moves as a threat.
scenes.visual: Los tres Sticks del mismo tamaño; el hilo rojo de la escena 304 los une; cada tarjeta de uno empuja la de otro en cadena.

scenes.headline: ONE BUILDING
scenes.text: In 1979, one flag came down in Tehran and another went up. From that day, the two conflicts became linked, and they have not come apart since.
scenes.visual: Vuelve el edificio de Teherán al atardecer; la bandera ondea; la cámara se aleja hasta el mapa de toda la región.

scenes.headline: YOUR TURN
scenes.text: That was the entire story, from 1948 to today, told from every side. Which chapter should we explain in more detail? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe for the next one.
scenes.visual: Stick WarMap señala los nueve capítulos en fila; botón SUBSCRIBE.
